reference.title: Dumbbell Shrug
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Back, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you shrug, hold briefly, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 1 s hold, 1.5 s down

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; stop about 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3)
prescription.progression: Add load, then a longer hold at the top

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width, dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in, arms long.
Breathe out and lift the shoulders straight up toward the ears.
Pause at the top for a second; arms stay straight.
Breathe in and lower slowly to a full stretch.

mistakes.fix: Move straight up and straight down.
Keep the arms long; let the shoulders do the lifting.
Keep the chin tucked and the neck long.

kinematics.norm: Shoulders rise straight up as far as comfortable (clinical opinion)
Arms by the sides; about 30 degrees of abduction is a variation that raised trapezius activity (Pizzari 2014)
About 1 s up, a 1 s hold and a slower lowering (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Ekstrom, Donatelli & Soderberg 2003, surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 33(5):247-258)
Pizzari et al. 2014, modifying a shrug exercise can facilitate the upward rotator muscles of the scapula (Clin Biomech 29(2):201-205)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The dumbbell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Neck pain or headache: use a lighter load and a smaller range.
modify: Shoulder pain: try the dumbbells slightly out from the sides.
Grip fatigue: use straps or lighter dumbbells.
progressions: Shrug with the arms about 30 degrees out to the side (Pizzari 2014).

muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Elevate the shoulder girdle. A shoulder shrug produced the greatest upper trapezius EMG of the exercises tested by Ekstrom 2003; shrugging with the arms about 30 degrees out to the side raised upper and lower trapezius activity further (Pizzari 2014).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Elevate the shoulder girdle. A shoulder shrug produced the greatest upper trapezius EMG of the exercises tested by Ekstrom 2003; shrugging with the arms about 30 degrees out to the side raised upper and lower trapezius activity further (Pizzari 2014).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Rhomboids (with levator scapulae, not shown) help elevate and steady the shoulder blade.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Rhomboids (with levator scapulae, not shown) help elevate and steady the shoulder blade.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the dumbbells; grip is often the limit with heavy shrugs.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the dumbbells; grip is often the limit with heavy shrugs.
